```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const container = DOM.element("div", { style: "height:460px;border-radius:6px;" });
  yield container;
  const map = L.map(container).setView([15, 10], 2);
  L.tileLayer("https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", {
    attribution: "© OpenStreetMap contributors"
  }).addTo(map);
  places.forEach(p => {
    L.marker([p.lat, p.lng]).addTo(map).bindPopup(`<b>${p.name}</b><br>${p.note}`);
  });
}
```

I will add a short story, dates, and photos to each of these once I'm able to
retrieve them — turning this section into a proper travelogue rather than
just a list of pins. In the meantime, what I can say is this: every one of
these places has taught me something. Working and traveling across such
different corners of the world — from research stations in West Africa to
conference halls in Europe, from field sites in Brazil to a new life in the
United States — has meant constantly encountering people whose experiences,
assumptions, and ways of solving problems look nothing like my own. That
exposure has shaped how I think as a scientist just as much as any dataset
or model has: it's taught me to ask better questions, hold my conclusions
a little more loosely, and stay curious about perspectives I haven't
considered yet.
